mcqs.q: Prosthodontics is the dental specialty concerned with:
opts: Diagnosis, treatment planning, rehabilitation and maintenance of patients with missing/deficient teeth or maxillofacial tissues
Only the treatment of gum disease
mcqs.explain: Prosthodontics restores oral function, comfort, appearance and health using biocompatible substitutes.

mcqs.q: The three main branches of prosthodontics are:
mcqs.explain: Removable, fixed and maxillofacial prosthodontics are the three branches.

mcqs.q: Removable prosthodontics is concerned with substitutes that are:
opts: Readily removable from the mouth by the patient
mcqs.explain: Removable prostheses (complete/partial dentures) can be taken out and replaced at will.

mcqs.q: A patient with NO remaining natural teeth is described as:
mcqs.explain: Edentulous = without teeth; treated with a complete denture. Dentate/dentulous = teeth present.

mcqs.q: A partially edentulous space may be restored by all of the following EXCEPT:
mcqs.explain: A complete denture replaces the ENTIRE dentition of a jaw; partial spaces are restored by RPD, FPD or implant.

opts: An artificial replacement of an absent part of the human body
The art and science of making replacements
mcqs.explain: Prosthesis = the artificial replacement itself; prosthetics = the art/science of supplying them.

opts: An artificial substitute for missing natural teeth and adjacent tissues
A cemented crown on a single tooth
mcqs.explain: A denture replaces missing natural teeth and their adjacent tissues.

mcqs.q: A fixed partial dental prosthesis (FPD) is one that is:
opts: Cemented to natural teeth, roots and/or implants
Removed and replaced by the patient at will
mcqs.explain: An FPD (bridge) is cemented and not patient-removable; an RPD is removable at will.

opts: The entire dentition and associated structures of one jaw
mcqs.explain: A complete denture replaces the whole dentition and associated structures of the maxilla or mandible.

mcqs.q: The impression (intaglio) surface of a complete denture is the part that:
opts: Has its contour determined by the impression and faces the tissues
Is polished and shows the buccal/lingual tooth surfaces
mcqs.explain: Impression/intaglio surface is shaped by the impression and seats against the tissues.

mcqs.q: The occlusal surface of a denture is the portion that:
opts: Is polished on the cheek side
mcqs.explain: The occlusal surface contacts the opposing denture/teeth.

mcqs.q: Denture RETENTION is the resistance to movement of the denture:
opts: Away from its tissue foundation, especially vertically
On its foundation against lateral forces
mcqs.explain: Retention resists vertical dislodgement away from the tissues; stability resists lateral movement; support resists seating toward the tissues.

mcqs.q: Denture STABILITY is the resistance of a denture to:
opts: Movement on its foundation, especially to lateral (horizontal) forces
Vertical dislodgement away from the tissues
mcqs.explain: Stability resists horizontal/lateral movement on the tissue foundation.

mcqs.q: Denture SUPPORT is the quality that resists movement of the denture:
mcqs.explain: Support resists vertical seating forces toward the tissues; broad load distribution is the 'snowshoe effect'.

mcqs.q: The 'snowshoe effect' in complete dentures refers to:
opts: Distributing masticatory forces across all the resilient supporting tissues
Concentrating forces on a single point
The cooling of the denture base
mcqs.explain: Like a snowshoe, the denture spreads load broadly over the tissues, aiding support.

saqs.q: Define prosthodontics and name its three branches.
saqs.a: Prosthodontics is the dental specialty concerned with the diagnosis, treatment planning, rehabilitation and maintenance of oral function, comfort, appearance and health of patients with missing/deficient teeth and/or maxillofacial tissues, using biocompatible substitutes. Branches: removable, fixed and maxillofacial prosthodontics.

saqs.q: Differentiate between edentulous, dentate, and partially edentulous, and give a treatment option for each partial space.
saqs.a: Edentulous = no natural teeth present (treated with a complete denture). Dentate/dentulous = natural teeth present. Partially edentulous = one or more (but not all) teeth missing, restored with a removable partial denture (RPD), a fixed partial denture (FPD), or a dental implant.

saqs.q: Define: prosthesis, denture, and complete denture.
saqs.a: Prosthesis = an artificial replacement of an absent part of the human body. Denture = an artificial substitute for missing natural teeth and adjacent tissues. Complete denture = a removable prosthesis that replaces the entire dentition and associated structures of the maxilla or mandible.

saqs.q: Name and describe the three surfaces of a complete denture.
saqs.a: 1) Impression (intaglio) surface — contour determined by the impression; faces the tissues. 2) Polished surface — the polished part of the base including the buccal and lingual surfaces of the teeth. 3) Occlusal surface — the part that contacts the antagonist (opposing) denture/teeth.

saqs.q: Compare denture retention, stability and support.
saqs.a: Retention resists movement of the denture AWAY from its tissue foundation (especially vertical). Stability resists movement ON the foundation, especially against lateral (horizontal) forces. Support resists movement of the denture TOWARD the tissues (vertical seating forces), aided by broad load distribution (snowshoe effect).
